extraction.name: WebWalkerQA
extraction.description: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal. It evaluates the capacity of LLMs to traverse a website's subpages to extract high-quality data systematically. The benchmark consists of 680 question-answer pairs from four real-world domains (conference, organization, education, and game) across over 1373 webpages. It includes both single-source and multi-source QA types, and is bilingual (Chinese and English), reflecting real-world web environments.
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang (Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group)
extraction.citeAs: Wu, J., Yin, W., Jiang, Y., Wang, Z., Xi, Z., Fang, R., Zhang, L., He, Y., Zhou, D., Xie, P., & Huang, F. (2025). WebWalker: Benchmarking LLMs in Web Traversal. arXiv:2501.07572.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected using a two-stage funnel annotation strategy combining LLM-based and human annotation. In the first stage, GPT-4o performs initial annotations by recursively traversing official websites, collecting information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages, constructing queries based on page information, and verifying/filtering for legitimate queries. In the second stage, crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control and filtering to refine the final results. Root pages were initially identified through Google search using keywords such as 'conference official website' or 'game official website', followed by manual filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains. Root pages were identified via Google search and manually filtered. For the education domain, official websites of various university computer science departments were chosen. Subpages were collected by systematically clicking and collecting subpages accessible through sublinks on the root page.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Queries were categorized into single-source and multi-source types based on whether information from one or multiple web pages is required. Difficulty levels (easy, medium, hard) were assigned based on the depth index value of the subpages involved. Multi-source QAs are labeled as multi_source_i where i represents the sum of depths of the two associated subpages, and single-source QAs are labeled as single_source_i where i denotes the depth of the corresponding subpage.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Step 1: Traverse official websites recursively, collecting information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages. Step 2: Construct queries based on the provided page information and specified role. Step 3: Verify and filter for legitimate queries that deviate from natural, human-like phrasing, retaining only QA pairs with short answers containing entities. Web pages were parsed into Markdown-like format using the ai4crawl tool. Clickable HTML buttons and corresponding URLs were extracted using Beautiful Soup.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A two-stage annotation process was used. Stage 1 (LLM-based): GPT-4o generates synthetic QA pairs from collected web page content using predefined prompts for both multi-source and single-source data. A verification step filters out queries that are unnatural, have long answers, or do not require combining information from multiple sources. Stage 2 (Human): Crowd-sourced human annotators rewrite and calibrate the questions and answers to ensure QA pairs are correct and consistent.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: GPT-4o (for LLM-based annotation); crowd-sourced human annotation platform (specific platform not named)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: GPT-4 is used as the evaluator to determine the correctness of responses by comparing predicted answers with ground truth using a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategy. The evaluation prompt instructs the evaluator to grade answers based on factual accuracy, ignoring differences in punctuation and phrasing, and allowing answers that contain more information than the true answer as long as there are no conflicting statements.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o (for initial QA pair generation and verification); GPT-4 (for evaluation); Beautiful Soup (for extracting clickable HTML buttons and URLs); ai4crawl (for converting web pages to Markdown-like format)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The WebWalkerQA dataset will be available at HuggingFace Datasets. The code of WebWalker will be released on GitHub at https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/WebAgent. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: WebWalkerQA addresses the limitation of traditional search engines that perform only horizontal searches and may not effectively trace deeper content embedded within websites. By enabling LLMs to perform deep, vertical web traversal, the benchmark supports more reliable and authoritative information retrieval from official sources, which has implications for improving AI-assisted information seeking in real-world scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is built on official websites in four specific domains (conference, organization, education, game), which may not represent the full diversity of web content. The language distribution is skewed, with Chinese accounting for 60.5% and English for 39.5%. Domain distribution is also uneven: education (46.3%), conference (24.0%), game (21.9%), organization (7.9%).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset size is limited to 680 high-quality QA pairs due to the complexity of queries in the web-agent domain. The dataset only utilizes HTML-DOM to parse clickable buttons and does not incorporate visual modalities such as screenshots. WebWalkerQA is built on official websites with dynamically updated information, meaning pre-trained models relying on static knowledge with a cutoff date may perform poorly. The benchmark currently covers only four domains and two languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: WebWalkerQA is designed for benchmarking and evaluating LLMs on web traversal tasks, specifically their ability to navigate multi-layered websites and extract information for question answering. It can be used for: (1) Testing and evaluation of LLM-based web agents; (2) Benchmarking RAG systems on deep web information retrieval; (3) Evaluating multi-step reasoning and information-seeking capabilities. The approximately 14k silver QA pairs (not yet human-verified) can serve as supplementary training data to enhance agent performance.
